newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MORE TROUBLE FOR CRISIS-HIT BRIGHTON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MORE TROUBLE FOR CRISIS-HIT BRIGHTON.

text.p: Crisis-hit English soccer club Brighton may have points deducted and be ordered to play a match behind closed doors following crowd disturbances this week.

The English Football Association (F.A.) charged the club which was in the F.A. Cup final 13 years ago but which is now facing possible extinction, with failing to control spectators during their third division clash with Lincoln on Tuesday.
Before the match supporters asked for it to be postponed because of the risk of crowd trouble.
About 50 Brighton followers charged on to the pitch after Lincoln scored, and the players had to retreat to the safety of the dressing-rooms.

The supporters then sat in the centre circle and were joined by another 100 fans from other parts of the ground. After a seven-minute protest they returned peacefully to the stands and play resumed five minutes later.
Brighton, F.A. Cup finalists in 1983, lost the match 3-1. There was another invasion at the final whistle by around 50 fans protesting against the club's beleaguered board.
The F.A. may now invoke a suspended sentence hanging over the club since April when serious crowd disturbances forced the abandonment of a game against York.
Brighton would then have three League points deducted and would have to play one match in an empty stadium.
The club has 14 days to appeal against Friday's charge.
Brighton are facing an extremely uncertain future because they must leave their ground, which has been sold to property developers, at the end of the season and they have no new ground to go to.
Much of the crowd's anger has been directed at owner Bill Archer who is refusing to sell the club to a local consortium.
